en: The Tathāgata’s Sūtra of Skillful Means and Mantras, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was on the summit of Mount Kailāsa, among the devas.
He was dwelling in a hermitage of sages,
together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus,
as well as an assembly of five hundred great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Their names were Maitreya Bodhisattva,
Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva,
and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Anantapuspa, the Bodhisattva Samantapuspa, and all these other bodhisattvas,
who have all reached the stage of being "born only once more" (ekajātipratibaddha) before succeeding to the position of a Buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One was in that grove,
surrounded by the great assembly before and behind him.
Then, a certain bhikṣu was possessed by a ghost.
His body was naked and he was unaware of it;
raising his hands, he cried out with coarse and vulgar speech.
Furthermore, another bhikṣu stood with his back turned to the Buddha in a state of perversion.
In the midst of the void, they cried out "Alas! with no self-mastery.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, having seen and heard this, immediately rose from his seat.
Baring his right shoulder and placing his right knee on the ground,
he joined his palms toward the Buddha and addressed him, saying: "World-Honored One,
who is it that makes this sound in the midst of the void?"
"Who has done this, and by what causes and conditions?
This one bhikṣu stands with his body exposed, raising his hands and crying out.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, saying:
"Good son, one bhikṣu has been seized by an evil spirit,
while another bhikṣu is possessed by a malevolent demon.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One, Tathāgata, out of compassion for all sentient beings today,
and for the sake of eliminating all suffering from illness,
you should proclaim this divine mantra.
At that time, by means of his supernormal powers,
the World-Honored One caused six Tathāgatas to suddenly appear in the midst of space, each of whom spoke a mantra.
The first is named Vipaśyin Buddha;
the second is named Śikhin Buddha;
the third is named Viśvabhū Buddha.
The fourth is named Krakucchanda Buddha;
the fifth is named Kanakamuni Buddha;
the sixth is named Kāśyapa Buddha.
At that time, Vipaśyin Buddha remained suspended in mid-air for the sake of protecting all sentient beings and for the purpose of eliminating all evil and malevolent spirits.
And he spoke this mantra:

1. Namo buddhāya 2. Namo dharmāya 3. Namo saṃghāya 4. Oṃ 5. Harā harā hile hile hila-ye 6. Nammo kṣele kṣila-ye 7. Jaganmo jñāna-ye 8. Namo nāma svāhā At that time, after Vipaśyin Buddha had spoken this mantra, [he continued].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"Good son, if there are faithful laymen or faithful laywomen who are able to receive, maintain, read, and recite this dhāraṇī..."
No weapons or staves can inflict harm upon them;
they cannot be harmed by fire or water;
non-humans and malevolent spirits cannot invade or afflict them, and they shall never meet with an untimely death.
If one has been poisoned by medicine, it will transform into delicious food that is easy to digest and free from illness.
When wishing to eat, first take a spoonful and recite the mantra over it seven times;
only then should one eat.
It can eliminate all curses and malevolent enchantments;
all illnesses shall be healed and cured; one’s lifespan will be extended;
whatever is heard by the ears will be remembered without forgetfulness; and during sleep, one will see the Buddhas in dreams.
If there is another person who has been afflicted by malevolent spells or sorcery,
one should recite this mantra seven times near their ear;
once that person has heard it, they will immediately be healed.
Furthermore, if there is anyone afflicted by epilepsy or white leprosy,
one should take *sumana* flowers and infuse them into sesame oil.
Take *agaru* (sandalwood), blue lotus, and *uragasāra* (spikenard);
take equal portions of each and grind them into a powder.
Mix this with oil and fry it, reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
When it is applied to the body, [the ailment] is immediately cured;
it can eliminate all manner of diseases.
At that time, Śikhin Buddha was dwelling in the void.
In order to protect all sentient beings,
to eliminate all illnesses, and to sever the influence of all ghosts and malevolent spirits,
this divine mantra is spoken.

Namo buddhāya (1). Namo dharmāya (2). Namo saṃghāya (3). Namo śikhine tathāgatāya (4). Oṃ (5). Vajra vajra (6). Vajrāya (7). Sarvabuddha-nam (8). Candra-rāja (9). Prabhite (10). Svāhā (11). At that time, the Tathāgata Śikhin, having spoken this mantra, [passed away].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, saying:
"Good son, this dhāraṇī has been spoken by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas."
I now speak it as well,
out of a desire to have compassion for all sentient beings,
to eliminate all illnesses, and to repel all malevolent spirits.
As well as various evil dreams, untimely deaths, and other such calamities.
Ākāśagarbha, if any son of good family or daughter of good family is able to recite and maintain this divine mantra while mindful of it day and night, [they shall be protected].
They shall never be afflicted by malignant diseases,
nor possessed by evil persons; while asleep,
they shall see the Buddhas in their dreams.
If, at the time of casting off the body, one encounters that Buddha,
one will attain the realization of the Way in his presence.
Such is the immeasurable power of this *dhāraṇī*, the Gaganagañjā.
I shall now explain it further for you in brief:
if there are good sons or good daughters who wish to sever all illnesses.
One should take threads of five colors and tie them into a mantra-cord.
If there is an epidemic, one should take *sumana* flower oil and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times.
If one applies it to the body, it will be immediately cured.
If one wishes to protect oneself and ensure peace and security,
one should recite the mantra over water one hundred and eight times.
Scatter [the materials] in the four directions to bind the boundary field (*sīmābandha*).
Take five-colored threads and tie them into a consecrated cord (*mantra-sūtra*) to wear.
For children possessed by malevolent spirits:
Take blue threads and tie them together to form a mantra-cord.
If one encounters affliction or confusion caused by evil and heterodox influences such that one loses consciousness,
recite this dhāraṇī near the person's ear.
Reciting this up to seven times will result in immediate recovery.
In all such matters, it may be used according to one's wishes.
At that time, Viśvabhū Buddha was dwelling in the void.
In order to protect all beings, to eliminate all their sufferings of illness,
and to sever the influence of all malevolent spirits,
he spoke this dhāraṇī.

1. Namo buddhāya. 2. Namo dharmāya. 3. Namo saṃghāya. 4. Namo viśvabhū-tathāgatāya. 5. Oṃ. 6. Karaka ra karaka. 7. Kurulu kurulu. 8. Kurucā mahāpuruṣa. 9. Kurusarvagaruḍa. 10. Svāhā. At that time, after the Buddha Viśvabhū had spoken this mantra, he said:
He addressed the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"Good son, this dhāraṇī belongs to all the Buddhas who appear throughout the Bhadrakalpa."
All the Buddhas of the three periods of time have fully expounded it;
I now expound it as well.
Ākāśagarbha, you should protect and uphold it.
If there are good men or good women who receive,
uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī,
they cannot be harmed by any blades or weapons.
No poisonous venom whatsoever can cause harm;
all fevers and malarial diseases shall be kept far away;
water cannot sweep them away, and fire cannot burn them.
They shall never die an untimely death,
nor shall any evil diseases be able to afflict them,
except for those results fixed by past karma.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās,
at the time of dawn they should bathe themselves clean and put on pure, clean garments; then,
before an image of the Buddha, they should burn fine and wonderful incense.
If one recites and maintains this mantra for one hundred and eight times,
all matters such as malevolent enchantments and curses will be unable to cause harm,
and all sufferings of illness will be completely dispelled.
All obstacles will be eliminated and one's lifespan will be extended.
All wealth and possessions will accord with one's desires, such that nothing will fail to be fulfilled.
Even if there are wicked people or malicious bandits, [they shall not cause harm].
The local officials and sovereign rulers anticipate their intentions and offer consolation;
thus, all sentient beings will be in accord.
Should there be any who face fear, strife, or confrontation with local authorities, [they shall find relief].
Take white thread and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Tie the enchanted cord and wear it;
the practitioner will achieve victory in all matters.
If one desires long life, take curd, honey, and rice blossoms and mix them together.
Using a spoon, scoop up the mixture and recite the mantra once before casting it into the fire;
repeat this up to one thousand and eight times, and one’s wish will then be fulfilled.
If one wishes to eliminate all obstacles for oneself and others,
to [attain] all wealth, treasures, and the like,
to be free from all evils, and to accomplish all skills and crafts:
Regarding the practice for upholding all mantras to subdue all enemies:
one should take *hrasva-gandha*, powdered incense, *śirīṣa* flowers, *tagara* incense, *śilāpuṣpa*, *kunkuma* incense, *vālaka*, and *indravāruṇī*.
Take equal parts of the white sap exuding from the branches of the tree and grind them into a powder.
Consecrate it by reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times.
By smearing it upon the body, one will immediately attain all that is desired.
If one wishes to see officials, high ministers, or others,
take a branch from a tree that exudes white sap and light a fire.
Recite the mantra once over a handful of sesame seeds.
Cast it into fire and burn it;
after doing this one thousand and eight times, one will obtain whatever one desires.
If one wishes to counteract poisons and medicinal drugs:
Before the image of the Buddha, smear the ground with clay.
Take one hundred and eight pieces of purple *karka* wood, each two inches long,
and place them inside clarified butter and honey.
Recite the name of each person one by one and cast it into the fire;
by reciting the mantra, one will immediately obtain their wishes.
If one wishes to eliminate all malevolent spirits, [one should do the same].
Take one hundred and eight embers from a funeral pyre where a corpse has been cremated.
Recite the mantra over each ember once and cast them into the fire; the affliction will be immediately cured.
This method may be employed in all such instances with equal success.
Except for cases where it would harm the bodies or lives of sentient beings,
at that time the Buddha Krakucchanda remained in mid-air to protect all sentient beings and eliminate all illnesses.
In order to sever all evils and malevolent spirits, he spoke this mantra:

1. Namaḥ buddhāya. 2. Namaḥ dharmāya. 3. Namaḥ saṃghāya. 4. Namo karakūṭāya. 5. Tathāgatāya. 6. Arhate. 7. Samyaksaṃbuddhāya. 8. Oṃ. 9. Kaṭa kaṭa kaṭa kaṭa. 10. Citi citi citi kāya. 11. Namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ. 12. Arhatparameṣṭhibhyaḥ. 13. Samyaksaṃbodhi-svāhā. At that time, after the Krakucchanda Buddha had spoken this mantra, [the assembly was established in peace].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"Good son, this dhāraṇī has been taught by as many Buddhas named Krakucchanda as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River."
Furthermore, it is that which has been spoken by all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
they praise and rejoice in it.
If there be a person who receives and upholds this divine mantra, [they shall obtain such merit].
In the future age, during the final kalpa,
they shall establish the Triple Gem and be able to give rise to right faith—
whether they be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās.
At the time of dawn, having bathed with purity and donned fresh, clean garments,
one should prepare various kinds of exquisite incense and flowers,
make offerings to the Buddha, and recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
That person will then be able to know the events of seven lifetimes;
if born in the heavens, they will become the most honored among the gods,
and if born in the human realm, they will attain the position of a sovereign over men.
If one can maintain this according to the Dharma until the end of life,
at the time of passing away, one will be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
If one can thus constantly recite and uphold it, [the same result shall follow].
In this very life, one shall be free from all various kinds of illness and suffering;
one shall obtain dhāraṇīs for retaining what is heard without forgetting.
If one desires food or drink, before it has even entered the mouth—
First recite the mantra seven times and then consume it;
by doing so, one will be free from all toxic diseases.
If one wishes to eliminate calamities and afflictions for others, [one should act in the same manner].
Recite the mantra over pure water one thousand and eight times;
use it to bathe the body before performing the rite.
If one is treating malignant sores, use a blade made of red copper.
If one recites the mantra seven times for such matters as these, they will immediately be fulfilled as desired.
If one can constantly recite and maintain it,
wealth and resources will come naturally, and all poisons will be destroyed.
All obstructing evil spirits, demons, and heterodox influences shall be entirely removed.
If one wishes to behold the body of the Buddha,
one should go to a pure place, whether it be a site of practice (bodhimaṇḍa) or before a stūpa.
Smear the ground with cow dung and burn aloeswood incense;
recite this mantra one thousand and eight times.
Lying down facing east, you will see the Buddhas in a dream.
Whatever their hearts desired was fulfilled without exception;
that Buddha-Tathāgata would immediately reveal to them whether their lifespan was long or short.
There may be some deficiencies;
all such matters were manifested in this way.
At that time, the Buddha Kanakamuni was dwelling in the void.
In order to protect all sentient beings from confusion and desolation,
to eliminate all illnesses, and to sever all evils and malevolent spirits,
this mantra is spoken.

1. Namo buddhāya. 2. Namo dharmāya. 3. Namo saṃghāya. 4. Namaḥ kanakamunaye. 5. Tathāgatāya. 6. Arhate. 7. Samyaksaṃbuddhāya. 8. Oṃ. 9. Sara sara sara sara. 10. Citrāpāye. 11. Dharma dharma dharma dharma. 12. Dūmo dūmo dūmaye. 13. Namaḥ kanakamunaye. 14. Tathāgatāya. 15. Arhate. 16. Samyaksaṃbuddhāya. 17. Siddhyantu mantrapadāni svāhā. At that time, after the Buddha Kanakamuni had spoken this mantra, he said:
He addressed the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"Good son, as for this dhāraṇī,
if there are good sons or good daughters..."
Those who are able to constantly read, recite,
receive, and uphold it will forever be free from fear and all enemies;
water cannot drown them, and fire cannot burn them.
If any poisonous substances are accidentally ingested,
they will be transformed into something sweet that sustains the body and prolongs life,
and there will be no calamities such as sudden illness or untimely death.
One's lifespan will be extended and one's official rank increased;
one will always be protected and mindful of by all Buddhas.
Should any obstacles arising from past karma manifest, [they shall be removed].
If one recites this three times a day, all ailments will be completely cured.
If one wishes to treat the diseases and sufferings of others,
one should provide food and drink according to one's means.
Furthermore, using various fragrant flowers or aloeswood incense (*agaru*) or frankincense (*guggulu*),
prepare pure and excellent water and recite the mantra one thousand and eight times over it.
Bathe the body with this water, and only then perform the recitation of the mantra.
All such sufferings of illness, as well as those possessed by evil and malevolent spirits, shall be completely cured.
This applies to the treatment of leprosy, bodily swellings, tumors, and diseases caused by wind and cold.
Take powdered achyranthes (chāngpú) and mix it with white honey.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times before the Buddha,
and when taken on an empty stomach, the ailment will be immediately cured.
If there are those suffering from malarial fevers lasting four days, three days, two days, or one day,
they should likewise smear the site of the ritual ground with cow-dung mud before the Buddha and take *sumana* flowers to fashion a garland.
If it is worn upon the head, one will immediately be freed from it.
If one is afflicted by malevolent sorcery (*yātudhāna*) to the point of fainting and losing consciousness,
if this mantra is recited one hundred and eight times at the side of the ear, one will immediately be cured.
If there are those suffering from ovine epilepsy or various forms of insanity,
or those possessed by *kāṭapūtana*, *piśāca*, and other such spirits,
one should smear the ground with cow-dung mud before an image of the Buddha.
As described above, having burned excellent and wondrous incense,
take the withered flowers previously offered before the Buddha and recite the mantra over them one thousand and eight times before burning them in the fire.
By fumigating the nostrils with it, one shall immediately be cured.
In all such illnesses, it should be applied according to the specific circumstances.

At that time, Kāśyapa Buddha, dwelling in mid-air for the sake of protecting all immeasurable sentient beings and for the purpose of eliminating all diseases, severing all evils, and dispelling all malevolent spirits, spoke this divine mantra.

1. Namo buddhāya. 2. Namo dharmāya. 3. Namo saṃghāya. 4. Namo kāśyapa-tathāgatāya. 5. Oṃ. 6. Hara hara hara hara. 7. Ha ha ha ha ha. 8. Namo kāśyapāya. 9. Arhatte. 10. Samyak-saṃbuddhāya. 11. Siddhyantu. 12. Mātṛ-pate. 13. Svāhā. At that time, after Kāśyapa Buddha had spoken this mantra, he said:
He addressed the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, saying:
"Good son, this dhāraṇī has been spoken by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in thirty-three Ganges Rivers."
"You should receive, uphold, recite, and practice it.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who recite this mantra three times during the day and night, [to the Bodhisattva] Ākāśagarbha..."
One will immediately attain the manifestation of seeing all Buddhas in dreams;
one shall be freed from all karmic obstacles,
with the sole exception of those retributions fixed by past lives.
In all matters, one may act according to one's wishes.
If one suffers from leprosy, white leprosy, or similar ailments,
one should do so before an image of the Buddha on ground smeared with cow dung and mud.
Having burned exquisite incense,
take all the withered flowers used for the Buddha's offerings and recite the mantra over them one thousand and eight times.
Grind it into a powder, mix with water, and drink it before the Buddha; one will immediately be cured.
This same method of treatment applies to chronic illnesses and various epidemics as well.
If one suffers from a headache, one should likewise apply the flower powder to the forehead.
If a woman experiences difficult labor, one should use the powder of this flower, mix it with oil, and fry it; then apply it to her female organ.
For such matters as these, there is no application according to the specific situation that does not bring benefit.
If there are scabies or moist ulcers, one should also use withered flowers.
Grind them into a fine powder, mix it with clarified butter (*sarpis*), and heat it over a fire.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times, then apply it to the sores; they will immediately heal.
If one wishes to stop the rain, one should also take withered flowers,
recite the mantra over them one thousand and eight times, and burn them on open ground;
by causing them to emit smoke, the sky will immediately clear.
If a great wind arises, or if there is thunder, lightning, and hail, these too shall be dispelled and ceased.
If one is afflicted by malaria that recurs every day, every two days, or even every four days,
one should likewise take withered flowers and recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Grind it finely into a powder and take it with wine; it will be cured immediately.
For those afflicted by "sheep-epilepsy" (ovine convulsions), recite the mantra over flowers as before;
whether burned or ingested, they shall all be healed.
If one is seized by yakṣas, piśācas, or various other spirits and ghosts,
or afflicted by diseases such as wind-cold disorders or lunar consumption,
one should drink it mixed with water.
For all such diseases as these, one should,
before the Buddha, upon a ground smeared with cow dung mud,
recite a mantra over a thousand and eight withered flowers.
Whether burned or ingested, all ailments shall be completely cured, and each person shall receive peace and happiness; do not harbor any doubts.
One should have resolute faith and employ it according to one's needs.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata was also in the sky.
In order to protect all immeasurable sentient beings,
to eliminate all illnesses, and to sever all evils and malevolent spirits,
this divine mantra is spoken.
1. Namo buddhāya. 2. Namo dharmāya.
3. Namo saṃghāya. 4. Namo śākyamunaye. 5. Tathāgatāya. 6. Arhate. 7.
Samyaksaṃbuddhāya. 8. Tadyathā: kumite kumite. 9. Mahākumite. 10. Tārite.
Li (10) mahāli (11) cili cili (12) mahācili (13) dāri dāri (14) mahādāri (15) tiri tiri (16) mahātiri (17) hahakīle kīle (18) mahākīle (19) julu.
Julu (20), mahājulu (21), mṛle mṛle (22), mahāmṛle (23),
tile tile (24), mahātile (25), dumbe dumbe (26), mahādumbe (27), cile cile (28).
Mahācāri (29) kṣiri kṣiri (30) mahākṣiri (31) cāle cāle (32) mahācāle (33) svāhā (34). At that time,
the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, having spoken this mantra, [remained silent].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, saying:
"Gaganagañja, if any son or daughter of good family receives,
maintains, reads, and recites this dhāraṇī..."
No weapons or staves can be brought against them;
neither water nor fire can harm them;
and no malignant diseases can afflict them.
They shall never meet with an untimely death.
This divine mantra, as spoken by the six Buddhas of the past, is no different from the others.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha...
He addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
I shall protect and uphold the divine mantras spoken by all the Buddhas as mentioned above."
I now likewise declare that it protects and sustains all immeasurable sentient beings;
it removes all obstacles, severs all karma,
extinguishes all transgressions, and eliminates all calamities.
It dispels all ghosts, repels all malevolent influences, and cures all diseases.
For these reasons, this divine mantra is spoken:
*Athakharali* (1), *Kakara* (2), *Bodhisattva* (3), *Mahāsattva* (4).
Bhagavati daśami trāyastriṃśatā | Ahamukhe bhagava upavane saḥ | Sarvīṣaṃ paripāpa | Cetyānām | Nirvāraṇi | Sarvabhyudgata | Nirvāraṇi | Saḥ ||
Bharuka 15, nibharaṇi 16, tadyathā 17, jili jili 18,
mahājili 19, dūlu dūlu 20, mahādūlu 21, sivale sivale 22, mahāsivale 23, ṅe.
24. *Mahā-ṅgali*; 25. *Svāhā*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha...
Having spoken this mantra, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, such a divine mantra possesses immeasurable spiritual power that is inconceivable."
If there are good men or good women who are possessed by evil spirits, they should fashion a mantra-cord from various threads and strands;
by reciting it one hundred and eight times, they shall wear it while walking or sitting.
Thereupon, those malevolent spirits will immediately depart.
Furthermore, take *sumana* flowers, pure cow ghee, white mustard seeds, and so forth,
mix them together in one place, and recite the mantra once for each time you cast them into the fire.
In this manner, one should repeat it up to one hundred and eight times;
by casting it one hundred and eight times, one will obtain healing.
If there should be an evil person who wishes to come and harm oneself...
Take a blade of tempered iron and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times over it;
then, wherever that evil person travels, they shall be unable to cause harm.
Alternatively, one may recite the mantra over water and scatter it in the four directions.
One should bind the boundary of the four directions and dwell within it;
then no evils whatsoever shall be able to inflict harm.
If one wishes to protect oneself so that no injury occurs, [one should do this].
Using threads of five colors, fashion a cord;
recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and wear it upon rising and sitting.
If you wish to remove poison, hold medicinal herbs in your hand and recite the mantra over them.
If one wishes to eliminate illness, one should consecrate oil with mantras one hundred and eight times; by applying it, one will be healed.
If one suffers from ear ailments, one should take *śrīveṣṭaka* (blue sandalwood).
Grind it finely into a powder and fry it in oil;
apply this into the ear.
If one suffers from abdominal ailments, recite the mantra over ginger-water one hundred and eight times and drink it; one will be cured immediately.
If one suffers from dental worms, wind-induced toothaches, or cavities,
take a branch of the *sumana* tree and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times;
then chew it with the mouth and rub it against the teeth, and they will immediately be cured.
For a child patient, one should tie white thread to form a consecrated cord (*mantra-sūtra*) for them to wear;
if the affliction is in the head, one may alternatively use a knife.
Alternatively, if one applies it to the hand and recites the mantra one hundred and eight times, one will immediately achieve recovery.
If one is possessed by a malevolent spirit, one should recite the mantra over a knife and use it to exorcise the affliction.
It can also be used to sever evil winds, hail, and rain.
Chant the mantra over a branch of a pomegranate tree and use it to ward off [evil].
Chant the mantra over water and use it to neutralize poisonous drugs.
In all such matters as these, employ them as you wish.
In all places, before an image of the Buddha, upon the earthen ground,
one should scatter flowers and burn incense, receiving and upholding [the rite] according to the Dharma.
Thus have these various Buddhas spoken this mantra-sūtra.
The Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, together with all the great bodhisattvas, arhats, and others,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced it accordingly.
Thus ends the *Tathāgata-upāya-kauśalya-mantra-sūtra*.
